comments.author: @privadovazquez4039
comments.text:
Indonesia is NOT “87% Muslim.” 

Indonesia is a huge and incredibly diverse country, made up of thousands of islands.

Places like Bali, Papua, and other regions have large Christian, Hindu, Buddhist, and other religious communities.

The official numbers often make Indonesia look more religiously uniform than it really is.

For example, Catholics are counted separately from Protestants, even though both are Christians. Together they amount to over 18%.

When you look at the different religious groups together, the non-Muslim population is much larger than many people realize.

There are also millions of Hindus and Buddhists, along with other religious communities such as Confucians. These groups amount to over 14%

So the important point is this:

🇮🇩 Indonesia is Muslim-majority, but it is also an extremely religiously diverse country and the number reported by government does not represent the reality.

And yes, because Indonesia has a population of more than 280 million people, it is the world's largest Muslim-majority country by population although most of this reality is more evident in Jawa.

The numbers are worth looking at carefully because percentages can sometimes hide just how diverse and developed Indonesia really is. They are more mature and modern than they appear to be.
